title: Robot Collisions
description:
There are `n` robots on a 1D line, each with a distinct initial position `positions[i]`, an integer health `healths[i]`, and a movement direction `directions[i]` (`'L'` for left or `'R'` for right). All robots start moving simultaneously at the same speed.

Whenever two robots meet at the same point, they collide:
- The robot with lower health is removed from the line, and the robot with higher health has its health decreased by `1` and continues moving.
- If both robots have the same health, both are removed from the line.

Return a list containing the final healths of all surviving robots in the exact order they appeared in the input (or an empty list if none survive).
constraints: All values in positions are distinct.
hints: Sort the robot indices by their starting position from left to right so collisions occur strictly between adjacent moving fronts.
Maintain a stack of indices of surviving right-moving robots; each left-moving robot collides with the top of the stack until it is destroyed or the stack becomes empty.

examples.explanation: All robots move right, so no collisions occur and healths remain [2, 17, 9, 15, 10].
Sorted by position: 2(R,15), 3(R,10), 5(L,15), 6(L,12). Robot at 5 destroys robot at 3 (becoming hp 14) then loses to robot at 2 (leaving hp 14); robot at 6 then loses to robot at 2, leaving [13].
Adjacent opposing pairs (pos 1 vs 2 with hp 10, and pos 5 vs 6 with hp 11) have equal health and destroy each other, leaving [].
